title: hymenophyllum hirsutum
intro: Hymenophyllum hirsutum, commonly known as the Hairy Marsilea, is a species of fern in the family Hymenophyllaceae. It is a perennial herb native to Australia and New Zealand, known for its unique, hairy fronds. The Hairy Marsilea has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which may aid in wound healing, reducing fever, and protecting against infections. The bioactive constituents of Hymenophyllum hirsutum include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and other secondary metabolites that exhibit therapeutic actions such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities.
